subject: physics
title: Nucleus Builder
summary: Grow a nucleus to its true radius, set the Coulomb hill two nuclei must climb and balance a radioactive decay.
concepts: Conservation of mass number and charge
learningOutcome: The student can find a nuclear radius from R₀A^⅓, find the Coulomb barrier Z₁Z₂e²/(4πε₀d) for two touching nuclei, and balance α and β decays with A and Z conserved.

levels.title: Clump’s radius
levels.adds: Baseline: R = R₀A^⅓ with R₀ = 1.2 fm, so the volume is proportional to A and the density is the same for every nucleus (Ex 13.4, 13.10; Example 13.1).
hints: Take the cube root of A, then multiply by 1.2 fm.
Doubling A multiplies the radius by only 2^⅓ = 1.26.
The radius ratio of two nuclei is the cube root of the ratio of their mass numbers.

levels.title: Climber’s hill
levels.adds: New idea: at touching the Coulomb energy is Z₁Z₂e²/(4πε₀d), which fixes the hill nuclei must climb to fuse (Ex 13.9).
hints: The centres are a distance d apart when the nuclei touch: add the two radii.
Give the answer in keV: multiply the MeV by 1000.

levels.title: Evo’s decay
levels.adds: Apply it: in a decay the mass number and the charge are both the same before and after, so the daughter follows from the particle that leaves (Example 13.4).
hints: An α-particle takes away A = 4 and Z = 2.
A β⁻ decay sends out an electron: A does not change, and Z goes up by 1. For β⁺, Z goes down by 1.
Check both sums: A_parent = A_daughter + A_particle and the same for Z.

levels.title: Nuclide twins
levels.adds: New: isotopes share Z, isobars share A and isotones share N; build the nuclide that matches the clue (Section 13.2).
hints: Isotope: same Z. Isobar: same A. Isotone: same N.
Use the clue’s extra fact to fix the other number.

misconceptions: Bigger nuclei are less dense than smaller ones
A nuclear reaction must have the same number of atoms of each element on both sides
A β decay changes the mass number
